replies.author: Mindestiny
replies.body:
Honestly, I think that's part of the charm.  Modern sports games give you the 1000 yard view, making you this omniscient team controlling sports God.  But... That's not how actually playing these games works.  The player has a limited field of view and opposing players right on their back.  There's tension in every play they make.

I think this perspective captures a little bit more of the "meat in the seat" perspective of play, you're making calls as if you were the player, not some omniscient coach.  If done well it could be a fresh take on the sports genre, less Sports Manager Sim and more Actually Playing Soccer.

Visually it's a bit of a throwback to the NES era of sports games too, kind of a retro vibe to the gameplay

comments.author: Mindestiny
comments.body:
Are you actually looking to develop a game, or are you looking to one shot some AI prompts and have this get spit out?  Those are two very different concepts.

For AI assisted development, Unity would be a great platform for this kind of game.  It does HD-2D pretty seamlessly (it's all just 3D, character sprites are 2D, the rest is lighting, camera, and stagecraft).  Assuming no dev knowledge, id start with the Unity tutorials on their site, get at least through Junior Programmer then start designing through something like Claude.

replies.author: Accurate_Cable_1372
replies.body:
So what you have is a simple web application. Meaning it uses the same things you would use to build a website which is totally fine. Lots of games do that.

Claude should help you with this, but at some point to make it a desktop app that you can send to people to play your game on their own computer, you’ll want to use this other tech called “Electron” which is basically just a web browser(Chrome-based) where you put your HTML/CSS/JS inside of and it will automatically run your game just like you would do in your browser.

It won’t look like a web browser and it won’t let your players visit other random websites within it but just know behind the scenes, that’s what it is. 

Then when you’re ready to release, you just upload that Electron application with your files setup inside of it.

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: You can do this with Unity, Godot or Unreal. Just requires a 3d scene, 2d character sprites (implemented in different ways depending on which engine, but generally this is a 2d sprite on a flat 3d mesh object.) It's really not hard to put into practice, even if getting the lighting to balance well between your sprites and 3d terrain can be a bit tricky, and it does mean you need to either have a limited camera rig or have your sprites animate for 5+ directions if free camera so that they can maintain their hd2d look when shifting view (based on angle of camera and the direction a character is meant to be facing relative to the camera you'd display a different animation set for them.)
